clue.text: Churchwoman's long passage

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church, followed by ANNE, a woman's name

explanation.surface: A female cleric is described as having a lengthy corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchwoman' splits as CH (church) plus ANNE (a woman), and the 's is just a joining 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel is a narrow waterway or route, such as the English Channel, a sea passage.

clue.text: Where a trumpet might once have been placed for better sound?

definitions.text: Where a trumpet might once have been placed for better sound?

parts.words: Where a trumpet might once have been placed for better sound
parts.note: the trumpet is not the brass instrument but an old ear trumpet, held to one side of the head to help hearing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a musician finding a better spot to play; the trumpet is the old hearing aid, and the phrase usually means something heard and instantly forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet was held up to a single ear of the hard-of-hearing listener, which is literally where it was placed.

clue.text: Weight of American's male organ

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a newspaper is an organ, and FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A crude question about how heavy a man's private parts are, apparently in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' points to the body but means a newspaper, here the Financial Times. 'American's' flags that this sense of the answer is chiefly US usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Heft is the heaviness or bulk of something, a mainly American word for its mass.

clue.text: It can pick up five from hotel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a microphone, which picks up sound
second meaning: in the phonetic alphabet the code word for M, five letters on from H (Hotel)

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a car collecting five guests at a hotel. Count H, I, J, K, L, M in the radio alphabet: five steps from Hotel lands on the code word for M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mike is an informal name for a microphone, the device that picks up sound for recording.

clue.text: Flapper maiden's skill isn't noticed at first

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over; the 's is 'has'
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: at first tells us to take the opening letters of the words isn't and noticed

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper girl's talent goes unappreciated to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' looks like a jazz-age young woman, but it is a bird that flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A martin is a small swallow-like bird, so jokingly something that flaps its wings in flight.

clue.text: Big organisation involved in high tension chase

indicators.note: involved in means the organisation's letters sit within the tension letters

parts.note: HT is the electrical abbreviation for high tension
the UN, the United Nations, is a very big organisation

explanation.surface: A large body is caught up in a tense, high-stakes pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt is to pursue or chase, as a noun a pursuit of quarry.

clue.text: Island north of Australia was aware of one of Thatcher's ministers, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read, giving words that sound the same

parts.words: was aware of one of Thatcher's ministers
parts.note: was aware of gives KNEW, and Leon Brittan served in Margaret Thatcher's cabinet as Home Secretary

explanation.surface: Someone knew of a Thatcher-era minister, and that is linked to an island near Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Leon Brittan was Home Secretary and Trade Secretary under Margaret Thatcher; said aloud with 'knew', his name gives the island.
explanation.definitionFit: New Britain is the largest island of the Bismarck Archipelago, part of Papua New Guinea, lying north of Australia.

clue.text: Drain beer and have toast

indicators.note: to drain a glass is to empty it, so the word beer loses its inside and keeps its ends

parts.note: to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a pint and raises a glass to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' at the end looks like a drinks toast after the beer; it is the verb for browning bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To brown food under a grill is to toast it, colouring its surface by heat.

clue.text: Opera North's English language influencer

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An opera company in the north of England is shaping how English is spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera North is a real Leeds-based company, which hides the split into Bellini's opera and N.
explanation.definitionFit: After 1066 the French of the Norman conquerors fed thousands of loanwords into English, reshaping its vocabulary.

clue.text: Left stuck in bowels of rustic laboratory, blending remedies

indicators.note: bowels are the innermost parts, so take the central two letters of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: Someone is abandoned deep inside a country lab where cures are being mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word gives its middle pair: ST, RA, ND and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stranded has been abandoned with no way to leave, like a ship run aground.

clue.text: Renegade entity won a number of uranium protons

indicators.note: a renegade breaks from its side, so these letters desert their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel body has won something linked to a uranium figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium's atomic number is 92, meaning each of its atoms has that count of protons in the nucleus.

clue.text: Extract of benzene's tertiary compound

indicators.note: Extract of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about extracting a tertiary compound from benzene.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Insertion clue in Indy sent a man mad regularly

indicators.note: regularly says take letters at even intervals, here every fourth letter of the words that follow

parts.words: clue in Indy sent a man mad

explanation.surface: A clue in the Independent about an insertion drove some solver round the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: Count from the fourth letter of 'clue' and take every fourth letter after: E, N, E, M, A.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is fluid inserted into the rectum, a medical insertion.

clue.text: On entering NY museum, number one ace gets obsession

indicators.note: entering means the word on goes inside the museum's letters

parts.note: MoMA is the Museum of Modern Art in New York
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Once inside a New York gallery, a top expert becomes fixated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' goes inside MOMA after its M, giving MONOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Monomania is a fixation on a single idea or subject, an obsessive preoccupation.

clue.text: Unit 17 broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken aloud, so we want its sound-alike

parts.note: 17 down is CUT, and to cut grass is to mow

explanation.surface: A unit numbered 17 is on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 17 down, whose answer is a synonym of mow.
explanation.definitionFit: The mho is an old unit of electrical conductance, ohm spelt backwards, now called the siemens.

clue.text: Many letters could be the reason the postie wears gloves?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mass posting of letters, such as advertising

definitions.text: could be the reason the postie wears gloves
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as a phrase: the post is too hot to handle

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MAIL'S HOT and the postman needs gloves to carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailshot is a batch of promotional letters sent out together to many recipients.

clue.text: Victoria and Ade seen tumbling together, generating a lot of clicks

indicators.note: tumbling together means the two names are mixed into one jumbled heap

explanation.surface: Two people, Victoria and Ade, take a fall and draw plenty of online clicks.
explanation.walkthrough: The clicks seem to be web traffic; they are the clicks of a Geiger counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive source makes a Geiger counter crackle with rapid clicks as it detects radiation.

clue.text: Editing process changed "ultimately" to "primarily"

indicators.note: primarily, meaning in the first place, says to take the opening letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: An editor swapped the word 'ultimately' for 'primarily'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' looks like a last-letter signal, but it is only fodder; 'primarily' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut is a deletion made by an editor, removing material from a text or film.

clue.text: Fellow dined inside, enthused hollowly, and came out

indicators.note: inside means the fellow and dining letters sit within the next part
hollowly means the word enthused is emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to have dined is to have eaten, ate

explanation.surface: A man ate a meal indoors, gushed insincerely, and then left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollowly' empties enthused down to its two ends, and 'inside' sets the fellow and the dining inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that emanated flowed or issued out from a source, as light does from a lamp.

clue.text: Regressing, until I snottily coughed out lump of tissue

indicators.note: Regressing says the hidden letters are read backwards
coughed out says the letters are brought up out of the words before it, hidden there

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone coughs up a lump, snuffling and sniffing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'coughed out' as part of the definition, leaving the hidden step without a signal; it is the hiding indicator, and the definition is just 'lump of tissue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsil is a mass of lymphoid tissue at the back of the throat.

clue.text: Widget appropriate for hole in a hatch

indicators.note: for means the hole is swapped out and appropriate takes its place

parts.note: a hatch is a small door
O is a round hole
apt means appropriate or fitting

explanation.surface: A gadget suited to fitting a hole in a hatch.
explanation.walkthrough: In A DOOR one of the two O's is replaced with APT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor is a small device fitting one connector to another, a typical gadget.

clue.text: No longer worried about wind being heard, with special provision for excess

parts.note: to be over something is to have got past worrying about it

indicators.note: being heard means the word is spoken aloud, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a draught is a current of air

explanation.surface: Someone stops worrying about a breeze, with an extra allowance for overflow.
explanation.walkthrough: A draught is the British spelling of a draft of cold air; the two sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is an arranged allowance from a bank letting a customer spend more than the account holds.

clue.text: One of five infiltrating network for Arab, say

indicators.note: infiltrating means one of five gets inside the network's letters

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
a quin is a quintuplet, one of five born together

explanation.surface: A quintuplet worms their way into some organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: EE is a UK mobile phone company. 'Arab' is not a person but a horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse, so it is an example of an equine animal.

clue.text: More revolutionary Monroe film sacked artist

indicators.note: sacked means the artist's letters are thrown out
revolutionary means the film title is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Niagara is a 1953 film starring Marilyn Monroe
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A more radical Monroe film is made after an artist is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Niagara (1953) is the Monroe thriller set at the falls; 'revolutionary' turns its title round before 'sacked' removes the Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Again can mean additionally or furthermore, as in 'and again, there is the cost'.

clue.text: Society function at democratic partnership

parts.note: tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A society event held at a democratic alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a stand is the run-scoring partnership between two batters at the crease.

clue.text: Minor damage to surface from small blow

parts.note: a cuff is a light blow with the hand

explanation.surface: A light knock leaves a little mark on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuff is a scrape mark, slight surface damage like that on shoes or paint.

clue.text: 60% of navy vote for Cable

indicators.note: 60% of means keep three of the five letters of the navy word

parts.note: a fleet is a navy
X is the mark made when voting

explanation.surface: Most of the navy votes for a politician named Cable.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable was a Liberal Democrat leader, which makes 'Cable' look like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flex is a flexible insulated electric cable, the lead on an appliance.

clue.text: OAP racing around tree bearing enclosed fruit

indicators.note: around means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A pensioner sprints round a tree bearing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree' seems to be what the pensioner runs round, but it starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An angiocarp is a plant whose fruit is enclosed within a covering such as a husk.

clue.text: Take canal boat nearly all the way back

indicators.note: all the way back means the shortened boat is read in reverse
nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed canal boat

explanation.surface: Catching a canal boat for almost the whole return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab is to seize or take hold of something quickly.

clue.text: Notable feature of large article on bird talk

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tern is a seabird
to jaw is to talk at length

explanation.surface: A noticeable trait of a big essay about birdsong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' is a facial feature, as in a prominent long jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern jaw is a long thin protruding jaw, a striking facial trait.

clue.text: Reset meter in old Mitsubishi

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a gauge is to set it back to nought
second meaning: the Mitsubishi A6M ..., a Japanese wartime fighter plane

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests winding back the odometer of an old Mitsubishi car; the Mitsubishi is the WWII Zero fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To zero an instrument is to recalibrate it to nought, and the A6M was a famous Second World War fighter aircraft.
